activation.rationale: Zero real generation/feedback cycles have occurred. Every record under feedback/, references/evaluations/, and evals/real-output-corpus/entries/ is a synthetic or explicitly-marked placeholder used to prove the record shape, not operating evidence. Running a full system review before SUE-570 would evaluate the absence of a system, not the system, which is exactly the vanity-health failure this surface exists to prevent. This judgement is deliberately revisable: a future reviewer should re-declare it, not simply extend this one, once real operating evidence starts to accumulate.

dimensions.asks: Does V2 materially improve accepted output quality and adaptability, using real owner-reviewed evidence rather than only synthetic evals?
evidence_refs: feedback/index.json#records — 2 records total, both synthetic seed examples
evals/real-output-corpus/entries — 5 entries total, all synthetic or explicitly-marked placeholders per evals/real-output-corpus/README.md
evidence_sources: feedback/records — feedback-record.schema.json instances: signal=objective_quality, owner_verdict
feedback/index.json#records — derived per-record summary index
evals/real-output-corpus/entries — corpus-entry.schema.json instances: owner_verdict, dimensions.strong, dimensions.weak, reference_eligible
schemas/l1-review.schema.json#outcome — comparative PASS/REWORK/TIE/ABSTAIN outcome shape; no populated L1 review store exists yet
evals/rubric.json — L0 synthetic rubric baseline, structurally distinct from real owner-reviewed quality lift and never a substitute for it
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: No real owner-reviewed feedback or corpus entries exist yet — only synthetic/placeholder seed records that prove the schema shape, not system performance.
dimensions.interpretation: Every quality-relevant record currently in the repository was authored to demonstrate a schema shape, not to report a real owner judgement. There is no basis yet to say V2 is or is not lifting accepted quality.

judgement_rules.healthy: Multiple real owner-reviewed outputs (beyond the SUE-570 pilot) show accepted-quality improvement or materially distinct, integrity-preserving audience transformations, corroborated by L1 comparative PASS outcomes against relevant references, without synthetic-only evidence standing in for real review.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Real owner-reviewed evidence shows quality flat or declining despite added machinery, or a content-type/audience transformation cannot be shown materially distinct from another without an integrity cost.
judgement_rules.watch: Real evidence exists but is thin, mixed, or flat — e.g. the accepted/rejected ratio is not improving, or L1 REWORK outcomes recur on the same dimension without resolution.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once the SUE-570 pilot and subsequent real review have produced multiple owner-reviewed feedback and corpus entries with owner_verdict values other than unknown.

dimensions.asks: Is natural-language operation actually staying simple as the system grows, measured by clarification frequency, correction cycles, and cases requiring the owner to name internal files/schemas directly?
evidence_refs: schemas/examples/intent-blocked-clarification.example.json — a worked schema example, not a real intake record
evidence_sources: schemas/editorial-intent.schema.json#clarification — required/asked/resolution fields (0-3 question norm, resolution states)
schemas/examples/intent-blocked-clarification.example.json — illustrative shape only, not a real operating record
docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §4 natural-language interface principle this dimension is judged against
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: No durable, committed store of real per-task Editorial Intent records exists yet outside schema examples; clarification counts cannot be measured from repository evidence alone until real intake runs accumulate (see known_gaps).
dimensions.interpretation: The clarification contract exists and is well-specified, but no real intake session has left a durable record in this repository yet to measure against it.

judgement_rules.healthy: Clarification counts stay within the intake gate's own 0-3 norm across real tasks, the owner rarely names internal files/schemas, and correction cycles trend down or stay stable as the system grows.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: The owner must routinely make manual JSON/repository edits, or the agent recurrently fails to infer profile/routing despite sufficient stated intent.
judgement_rules.watch: Clarification counts creep upward, or the owner increasingly names internal artifacts (schema/skill/file names) instead of describing intent in natural language, without yet being structural.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once real natural-language intake sessions (starting with SUE-570) leave enough durable Editorial Intent evidence to count clarification frequency and correction cycles.

dimensions.asks: Does progressive disclosure hold as the repository grows, so a larger repository does not imply proportionally larger per-task context?
evidence_refs: schemas/visual-job.schema.json#context_isolation — an enforced allowlist, but not a measurement of how much context was actually loaded
evidence_sources: docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §9 context and cost budget principle
schemas/visual-job.schema.json#context_isolation — permitted_inputs/excluded allowlist, the one enforced context-scoping mechanism that exists today
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: No schema or record in this repository carries a token/context-size proxy field yet, so context load cannot be measured from committed evidence at all — a structural gap, not merely an observation gap (see known_gaps).
dimensions.interpretation: context_isolation proves a boundary is enforced on visual jobs; it does not measure how much context any task actually loaded. No schema in the repository currently records a context/token size, so this dimension has no quantitative evidence source at all yet, only a qualitative boundary contract.

judgement_rules.healthy: Per-task context/profile/reference loading stays roughly flat as the repository grows, matching the progressive-disclosure design; no whole-repo/full-history loading incidents are observed.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Per-task context load grows roughly with repository size, or whole-repo/full-history loading recurs.
judgement_rules.watch: Occasional unnecessary-context incidents occur but are isolated and quickly corrected.

dimensions.recommended_action: Do not add a new telemetry field to satisfy this dimension. Track whether a context/cost proxy lands on an existing record (per docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §9/§11's evidence table) via AES-V2.10 or a later job-record contract, and re-evaluate once it does.

dimensions.asks: Do references improve quality without the system's own outputs quietly becoming the default reference pool?
evidence_refs: references/index.json#by_provenance_class — external: 3, owner_created: 0, generated_output: 0 as of this snapshot
evidence_sources: references/index.json#by_provenance_class — external/owner_created/generated_output counts
references/index.json#promoted_generated_output — count of generated_output references actually promoted
references/evaluations — reference-evaluation.schema.json instances: provenance_class, promotion.evidence_refs, promotion.basis
schemas/l1-review.schema.json#anti_collapse — same-lineage GOOD-reference concentration flag
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: The reference pool is entirely external, small, and pre-operation, so no selection-under-pressure or self-reinforcement pattern can be observed yet.
dimensions.interpretation: Every reference evaluation currently in the registry is external and none has ever been promoted from a generated output. The anti-collapse concern this dimension exists to catch cannot yet be observed because generated_output references do not exist in the pool at all.

judgement_rules.healthy: The reference pool stays a healthy external/owner_created/generated_output mix, generated_output promotion always follows the evidence-backed protocol (never publication or an L1 pass alone), and the L1 anti-collapse flag never triggers on the operative comparison set.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Selected GOOD references concentrate on one generation lineage as the de facto default, or a generated_output reference is found carrying an adopt verdict without a valid promotion record.
judgement_rules.watch: generated_output references are accumulating faster than external/owner_created ones, or the anti-collapse flag has triggered at least once without a corrective change.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once generated_output references start entering the pool (post-pilot) and selection-in-production evidence exists to check for lineage concentration.

dimensions.asks: Is preference change handled as versioned, evidence-backed calibration rather than accumulating silently, and does calibration entropy stay bounded?
evidence_refs: calibration/versions — AES-V2.10 (SUE-568) is concurrent, in-progress work as of this snapshot; no durable decision has an operating history yet
calibration/ledger — no drift candidates raised-vs-approved history exists yet
evidence_sources: calibration/versions — durable calibration version records (AES-V2.10 / SUE-568)
calibration/ledger — experiment/drift ledger (AES-V2.10 / SUE-568)
docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §7 model drift as an editorial quality event; the learning boundary
schemas/feedback-record.schema.json#calibration_ref — links a feedback record to the calibration version active when it was made
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: No durable calibration decision has been activated and evaluated over time yet — early calibration/version records reflect initial authoring, not a tested decision with a change-frequency or reversion history.
dimensions.interpretation: Calibration versioning itself is being built concurrently with this evaluation surface. Whatever versions exist at any given moment reflect initial authoring, not a preference decision that has survived real use, reversion pressure, or contradiction with another active preference.

judgement_rules.healthy: Calibration changes are infrequent, each backed by repeated independent evidence or an explicit owner declaration (never a single complaint), with no reverted changes and no standing contradictions.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Calibration versions change frequently, changes get reverted, contradictory active preferences coexist, or profiles exist that are never exercised.
judgement_rules.watch: Drift candidates are being raised but not yet resolved, or a small number of profiles show early signs of low use.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once calibration/ledger shows drift candidates raised and either approved or rejected, and calibration/versions shows at least one version with real change-frequency history.

dimensions.asks: When output is bad, is it repaired at the correct layer on the first targeted attempt, without misrouting into polish, brand_profile, or a content rule?
evidence_refs: feedback/records — 2 synthetic seed records with routing decisions recorded, but no linked repair outcome
evidence_sources: feedback/records — routing.layer / routing.modality_layer / routing.abstained fields
schemas/feedback-record.schema.json#routing — the three-state routing contract (shared-layer / modality-only / abstention)
editorial/feedback-routing.json#authority_matrix — declared repair-layer authority classes
editorial/FEEDBACK-ROUTING.md — §3 tuning procedure: keep/revert/insufficient evidence
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: No feedback record traces a routing decision to an actual repair outcome yet — the schema has no revision/replan/rerender lineage field to link a routing.layer decision to whether the fix worked (see known_gaps).
dimensions.interpretation: The routing vocabulary and misroute detection are implemented and testable (scripts/lib/routing-core.mjs), but nothing in the repository yet records whether a routed repair actually resolved the failure it targeted. Routing correctness at intake time is not the same evidence as routing effectiveness over time.

judgement_rules.healthy: The first targeted repair at the identified layer resolves the failure in the large majority of real cases, reroutes/escalations are rare, and none of the three named misroutes (frame-in-polish, renderer-in-brand-profile, reference-in-content-rule) are observed.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: A named misroute recurs, first-repair success rate trends down, or Core/Constitution escalation is attempted from evidence that does not meet the class-4+ bar.
judgement_rules.watch: Reroutes/escalations happen occasionally, or one of the named misroutes is observed once and then corrected.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once revision/replan/rerender lineage lands on job/package records (owned by AES-V2.10 or a later contract, per known_gaps) and real routed-repair-then-outcome cases exist.

dimensions.asks: Do intent interpretation, Source/Reference handling, profile/audience/calibration interpretation, and feedback routing stay consistent across agents and model versions without large model-specific prompt forks?
evidence_refs: schemas/visual-job.schema.json#renderer — the field exists and is required, but no populated visual-job records exist yet to compare across runtimes
evidence_sources: docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §13 AES-V2.11 (SUE-569) certification, the intended primary evidence source for this dimension
schemas/visual-job.schema.json#renderer — provider/model/model_version runtime lineage recorded per job
schemas/feedback-record.schema.json#evaluator — evaluator.type / agent.runtime / model / version for an agent evaluator
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: SUE-569 certification has not yet run and no multi-agent/multi-model operating history exists in this repository to compare.
dimensions.interpretation: The lineage fields needed to observe cross-agent/model consistency exist on visual-job and feedback-record, but no populated records exist yet, and SUE-569 (the issue this dimension is explicitly keyed to) has not run.

judgement_rules.healthy: Intent interpretation, Source/Reference handling, profile/audience/calibration interpretation, and feedback routing stay consistent across agents/models, with no growth in agent-specific workarounds.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Large model-specific prompt forks are required to keep behavior consistent, or a model-version upgrade causes a routing/interpretation regression that recurs.
judgement_rules.watch: A small, explained set of agent-specific adapters exists but is shrinking or stable, not growing.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once SUE-569 certification runs and/or multiple populated visual-job or feedback records with distinct evaluator.agent.runtime/model values exist to compare.

dimensions.asks: Are write-authority boundaries actually holding in exercised cases — no local feedback silently promoted to durable preference, no mutation above authority class, no canonical/draft/publication boundary violation?
evidence_refs: scripts/lib/registry-core.mjs#checkOwnerVerdict — exists and is exercised by scripts/test-registry.mjs, but only against synthetic fixtures, not real operating cases
evidence_sources: schemas/feedback-record.schema.json#scope — task_local/calibration_candidate ceiling; no field exists for class 4+ by construction
scripts/lib/registry-core.mjs#checkOwnerVerdict — mechanically enforces silence-is-not-acceptance
editorial/feedback-routing.json#authority_matrix — the seven-class write-authority ladder
docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §10 write-authority ladder definition
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: Absence of evidence is not automatically PASS (SUE-573 explicit requirement): with almost no exercised operating history, there are simply not enough real cases to inspect for a violation either way.
dimensions.interpretation: The write-authority ladder and its mechanical guards are implemented and unit-tested. That is evidence the control exists, not evidence that it has been tested against a real boundary-pressure case. This dimension is deliberately not marked HEALTHY on the strength of an untested control — see judgement_rules and SUE-573's explicit 'absence of evidence is not automatically PASS'.

judgement_rules.healthy: No material incident or near-miss is found on inspection: no local feedback silently promoted to durable preference, no mutation above authority class, no unreviewed Core/SSOT change, no canonical/draft/publication boundary violation.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: An actual authority violation reached a durable artifact — a class-4+ change made without the required human authorization/review, or generated output promoted to Reference authority without evidence.
judgement_rules.watch: A near-miss is found and caught by an existing mechanical guard (e.g. scripts/lib/registry-core.mjs) with no actual boundary breach reaching a durable artifact.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate once real feedback/calibration/reference activity has actually exercised the authority ladder (i.e. a real attempt at a class-4+ change occurred and was correctly blocked or correctly escalated).

dimensions.asks: Is the system optimizing cost per accepted output, not raw generation-call count, and does cost change sensibly after a model/profile change?
evidence_refs: schemas/audio-plan.schema.json#cost — field exists, required, but no populated audio-plan records exist yet
schemas/visual-job.schema.json#attempts — field exists, but no cost_per_accepted_artifact equivalent exists on this schema yet
evidence_sources: schemas/audio-plan.schema.json#cost — renders_attempted/renders_accepted/cost_per_accepted_artifact; the one modality that already carries this field
schemas/visual-job.schema.json#attempts — attempts/max_attempts as a rerender-count proxy; visual-job has no cost_per_accepted_artifact field yet
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: No audio-plan or visual-job records are populated yet, and visual-job carries no cost_per_accepted_artifact field at all (see known_gaps) — there is neither data nor, for visual, a complete field to hold it.
dimensions.interpretation: Audio (deferred from the pilot per docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §13) already has the right field shape but zero populated records. Visual has operating attempts/max_attempts but no accepted-cost field at all, so cost per accepted result cannot be computed for visual outputs even once records exist.

judgement_rules.healthy: Renders/revisions per accepted artifact trend flat or down as profiles mature, per the audio-plan cost block (and any later visual-job equivalent).
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Cost per accepted artifact is rising, or a model/profile change measurably raised cost without a corresponding quality gain.
judgement_rules.watch: Cost per accepted artifact is roughly flat but not improving despite calibration/profile investment.

dimensions.recommended_action: Do not add cost_per_accepted_artifact to visual-job from this package. Flag it to the schema/contract that owns visual-job (per known_gaps) and re-evaluate once either audio-plan records populate or visual-job gains an equivalent cost block.

dimensions.asks: Does the repository stay understandable months later — is duplicated authority avoided, are exceptions bounded, and does one change stay scoped to a small, related file set?
evidence_refs: docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §12 names the concrete stop conditions this dimension will check against once there is enough history to check
evidence_sources: editorial — active authority documents under editorial/*.md, a rough proxy for architecture surface
schemas — active schema files under schemas/*.json
docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §12 'What V2 must not become' stop conditions, the direct judgement rubric for this dimension
docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md — §13 issue map, used to check whether one change requires touching too many unrelated files
dimensions.insufficient_evidence_when: The Core (V2.1-V2.11) has not finished landing and the Owner Playbook (SUE-571) does not exist yet, so there is no stable baseline to compare growth against.
dimensions.interpretation: Section 12's stop conditions give this dimension a real, checkable rubric, but checking it meaningfully requires enough elapsed history to see whether authority documents/schemas are accumulating faster than capability, which does not exist yet this early in the Core's own construction.

judgement_rules.healthy: The number of active authority documents/profiles/schemas is stable or shrinking relative to capability, no duplicated/overlapping rules are found, and one change typically touches a small, related file set.
judgement_rules.structural_risk: Identifying current authority requires cross-referencing many documents, a routine change now requires touching many unrelated files, or the Owner Playbook (SUE-571) no longer matches actual behavior.
judgement_rules.watch: New exceptions or agent-specific adapters are appearing, or a stale/superseded file is found but not yet cleaned up.

dimensions.recommended_action: Re-evaluate at the next major architecture change or at the V3 readiness gate (SUE-574), once SUE-571's Owner Playbook exists to compare against actual behavior.

known_gaps.description: schemas/feedback-record.schema.json has no field capturing whether a targeted repair actually resolved the problem, whether it required a reroute/escalation, or how many revision/replan/rerender cycles a task went through. routing.layer records the routing decision at the moment of feedback; nothing links it forward to the outcome of the repair it triggered.
known_gaps.owner_contract: Job/package lineage per docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §11's evidence table ('revision / replan / rerender lineage -> job and package lineage'), most likely landing via AES-V2.10 (SUE-568) or a later job-record contract. This package identifies the gap; it does not add the field.

known_gaps.description: Only schemas/audio-plan.schema.json carries a cost block (renders_attempted/renders_accepted/cost_per_accepted_artifact). schemas/feedback-record.schema.json, schemas/editorial-intent.schema.json, and schemas/visual-job.schema.json carry no token/context-size or reasoning-cost proxy at all.
known_gaps.owner_contract: Per docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §9 and §11's evidence table ('cost / context proxy -> job and review records'), owned by the job/review record contracts (e.g. a visual-job cost block mirroring audio-plan's) — not this package.

known_gaps.description: schemas/editorial-intent.schema.json is complete and has illustrative examples under schemas/examples/, but there is no committed per-task record store analogous to feedback/records/ or references/evaluations/ — so operator_friction (clarification frequency, correction cycles) cannot be measured from repository evidence alone.
known_gaps.owner_contract: AES-V2.1/V2.2 intake contract (SUE-559/SUE-560), or the SUE-570 pilot's own evidence capture — not this package.

trigger_note: First declaration of the system evaluation surface itself (AES-V2.14 / SUE-573). Authored before the SUE-570 pilot has run and before any real post-Core operating history exists — every record cited below is a synthetic or placeholder seed used to prove a record shape, not evidence of the system operating.
